paragraphs.text: Qing Mao Hong Cha is a loose [red tea](red:definition) from Yunnan, from the 2018 harvest.
The trade keeps Yunnan red [for freshness rather than for age](dian-hong:ageing), and looks to its first one to three years. At eight years this leaf is well past that window.

It belongs to the style sold as [Dian Hong](dian-hong:definition), made from the province's large-leaf trees. The leaf is [withered, rolled and left to oxidise](dian-hong:making) until it turns from green to reddish brown, then dried with heat to fix it.

brewing.text: Dian Hong takes hot water, roughly 90 to 100°C. A common start is about 5 grams to 100 ml, with short steeps that lengthen slowly as the leaf opens.

notice.text: A full, sweet cup, often described as malty, with chocolate or cocoa and honey notes and sometimes something floral. The liquor runs golden to bright red, and a good grade has little bitterness.
